info.description:
# E-tiGo API v1

**Ride-hailing platform API for Lagos, Abuja, and other Nigerian cities.**

## Quick Start

### 1. Environment Setup
Select **E-tiGo — Local** or **E-tiGo — Staging** from the Postman environment dropdown.

### 2. Seeded Test Accounts

All seeded accounts use the password: `Qwer!234`

#### Admin Accounts
| Email | Role | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `admin@etigo.com` | Super Admin | Default super admin account |
| `ops@etigo.com` | Operations | Operations manager |
| `safety@etigo.com` | Safety Operator | SOS/safety console access |
| `support@etigo.com` | Support | Customer support agent |
| `supportlead@etigo.com` | Support Lead | Tier 2 disputes, refund approvals up to ₦50,000 |
| `finance@etigo.com` | Finance | Finance & payments manager |

#### Passenger Accounts (OTP login)
| Phone | Email | Name |
|-------|-------|------|
| `+2348100000001` | `ade@demo.etigo.com` | Ade Ogunleye |
| `+2348100000002` | `ngozi@demo.etigo.com` | Ngozi Okafor |
| `+2348100000003` | `emeka@demo.etigo.com` | Emeka Nwosu |
| `+2348100000004` | `funmi@demo.etigo.com` | Funmi Adeyemi |
| `+2348100000005` | `chidi@demo.etigo.com` | Chidi Eze |

#### Driver Accounts (OTP login)
| Phone | Email | Name | Status | Vehicle |
|-------|-------|------|--------|---------|
| `+2348200000001` | `bayo@demo.etigo.com` | Bayo Akinola | Approved (Online) | Toyota Corolla (Economy, petrol) |
| `+2348200000002` | `kemi@demo.etigo.com` | Kemi Bakare | Approved (Offline) | Honda Accord (Comfort, hybrid) |
| `+2348200000003` | `segun@demo.etigo.com` | Segun Obaseki | Approved (Online) | Mercedes-Benz EQE (Premium, electric) |
| `+2348200000004` | `amara@demo.etigo.com` | Amara Nnamdi | Pending Review | Toyota Highlander (SUV, petrol) |
| `+2348200000005` | `tunde@demo.etigo.com` | Tunde Fashola | Suspended | Nissan Sentra (Economy, CNG) |
| `+2348200000006` | `ify@demo.etigo.com` | Ify Okoro | Rejected | — |

### 3. Seeded Data

#### Cities
Polygon boundaries around each city's built-up area (no overlaps); the server books the city the pickup lies in.

All 22 are live: Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Ibadan, Abeokuta, Ilorin, Ado-Ekiti, Akure, Enugu, Aba, Umuahia, Benin City, Owerri, Kano, Uyo, Warri, Asaba, Onitsha, Kaduna, Jos, Osogbo and Calabar.

Every city has local demo drivers (`<first>.<last>.<city>@ops-demo.etigo.com`, never offered real rides) and passengers (`<first>.<last>.<city>@demo.etigo.com`) with a few weeks of trips. Fares come in three tiers: Lagos and Abuja, large cities, other cities. See the API reference, Quick Start.

#### Vehicle Classes
| Class | Display Name | Capacity |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| economy | Economy | 4 |
| comfort | Comfort | 4 |
| premium | Premium | 4 |
| suv | SUV | 6 |

#### Promo Codes
| Code | Type | Value | Status |
|------|------|-------|--------|
| `WELCOME50` | 50% off (max ₦2,000) | Active | 1 use per user |
| `RIDE500` | ₦500 flat discount | Active | 3 uses per user |
| `OFFPEAK20` | 20% off (off-peak only) | Active | 5 uses per user |
| `EXPIRED10` | 10% off | Expired | — |
| `ILORIN500` / `COALCITY20` / `GARDENCITY15` / `BENINLAUNCH` | City promos (Ilorin, Enugu, Port Harcourt, Benin City) | Active | — |

#### Offline Trip Flags (compliance demo)
Run `php artisan db:seed --class=OfflineFlagsDemoSeeder` (non-production). 22 flags for 11 Lagos drivers cover every status (flagged, disputed, upheld, overturned) at every level, each with a route map and history. Drivers log in as `driver.compliance.<name>@ops-demo.etigo.com` (password `Qwer!234`) and stay offline.

| Driver | Try |
|--------|-----|
| Musa Garba | L3 past the driver's 48 h: Confirm Deactivation works |
| Funke Ajayi | L3 by verified cash-taking, inside the 48 h: Uphold/Confirm return 422 (except super admin) |
| Chidi Nwosu | L3 disputed: review the dispute, then confirm |
| Bisi Okonkwo / Ada Obi | Disputed L2 / L1 awaiting review |
| Segun Alabi | Deactivation confirmed: only a super admin can overturn (reactivates him) |
| Yemi Ogunleye | L2 overturned on appeal |
| Emeka Udeh / Tayo Bankole | Overturned L3 / L1 |
| Kola Adebayo / Ngozi Eze | Fresh L1 / upheld L1 + lapsed L2 |

Set `flag_id` from `GET /admin/offline-flags?search=<driver name>`.

#### EV station details (admin demo)
Run `php artisan db:seed --class=EvStationsDemoSeeder` (non-production). "Yaba EV Hub" in Lagos: Ifeoma Chukwu and Dapo Adeyemi charging at stalls 1 and 2 (stall 2 frees up first), stall 3 out of service, and Zainab Lawal, Obinna Okafor and Sade Ogunbiyi in the queue. All five drive electric cars, log in as `<name>.ev@ops-demo.etigo.com` (password `Qwer!234`) and stay offline. Re-running it resets the station relative to now. **List All Stations** with `search=Yaba` sets `ev_station_id`.

### 4. Authentication Flow

**Passengers & Drivers:** Send OTP → Verify OTP → (if new user) Complete Registration → Use bearer token.

**Admins:** POST `/admin/auth/login` with email & password → Use bearer token.

All protected endpoints require: `Authorization: Bearer {token}`

### Static OTP (Non-Production Only)

In **local** and **staging** environments, all OTP codes are **`123456`**. Message delivery is skipped entirely. This lets you create and verify accounts freely without OTP costs.

1. `POST /auth/otp/send` with any valid phone → returns success immediately
2. `POST /auth/otp/verify` with same phone + code `123456` → logs in or prompts registration

**Production always generates random codes and delivers them through Sendchamp: WhatsApp (approved OTP template) first, SMS fallback.**

### 5. Rate Limiting
Auth routes (`/auth/*`, `/admin/auth/*`) are rate-limited to **5 requests/minute** per IP. Exceeding returns `429 Too Many Requests`.



### 6. Admin Roles & Permissions

E-tiGo uses role-based access control (RBAC) for admin endpoints. Super Admins bypass all role checks.

| Role | Value | Access |
|------|-------|--------|
| Super Admin | `super_admin` | Full system access, admin management |
| Operations | `operations` | Drivers, cities, vehicle classes, pricing, surge, rides, monitoring, fleet (incl. shift mode and driver shifts), vehicle maintenance, availability coverage, gamification, promos, EV stations, offline flags, lost & found (queue and settings), operational reports |
| Safety Operator | `safety_operator` | SOS console, drivers, passengers, offline flags, disputes (Safety queue; reads all cases) |
| Support | `support` | Passengers, disputes (tier 1), lost & found, wallets (read-only), driver ledgers (read-only) |
| Support Lead | `support_lead` | Everything Support has, plus tier 2 disputes (escalations, appeals) and dispute refund approvals up to ₦50,000 |
| Finance | `finance` | Pricing, fleet, promos, wallets, ledger, adjustments, payouts, refunds, settings, all reports |

| Endpoint Group | Operations | Safety | Support | Finance |
|----------------|:----------:|:------:|:-------:|:-------:|
| Drivers (incl. vehicle class) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| Cities / Vehicle Classes / Surge | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Pricing | ✅ | — | — | ✅ |
| Rides (pending, assign) / Live Monitoring | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Rides (refund) | — | — | — | ✅ |
| Fleet Vehicles / Fleet Agreements | ✅ | — | — | ✅ |
| Gamification | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Promos | ✅ | — | — | ✅ |
| EV Stations | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Offline Trip Flags | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| SOS Console | — | ✅ | — | — |
| Passengers | — | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Disputes (support queue; Support Lead too) | — | view | ✅ | — |
| Disputes (Safety queue) | — | ✅ | — | — |
| Dispute refund requests | — | ✅ | ✅ (lead approves) | ✅ |
| Lost & Found queue | ✅ | — | ✅ | — |
| Lost & Found settings | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Driver Shifts / Availability Coverage | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Vehicle Maintenance | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Wallets (view) / Driver Ledgers | — | — | ✅ | ✅ |
| Wallets (freeze), Ledger, Adjustments, Payouts, Settings | — | — | — | ✅ |
| Reports (financial / reconciliation) | — | — | — | ✅ |
| Reports (operational) | ✅ | — | — | ✅ |
| Admin Management | — | — | — | — |

### 7. Variables & Request Chaining

Select an environment first. Login and registration requests store `passenger_token`, `driver_token` or `admin_token` automatically (in the active environment and the collection).

**Run these once before anything else** — they store the seeded ids the other requests use:

1. **Public → List Active Cities** → `city_id` (Lagos)
2. **Public → List City Vehicle Classes** → `economy_class_id`, `comfort_class_id`, `premium_class_id`, `vehicle_class_id`

Other requests store ids as you go: **Create Ride** → `ride_id`, `share_token` · **Top Up Wallet** → `topup_reference` · **Initialize Payment** → `payment_reference` · **List All Drivers** → `driver_id`, `driver_user_id` · **Available Drivers for Ride** → `driver_user_id` · **Get Driver** → `document_id` · **List Wallets** → `account_id` · **Request Payout** → `payout_id` · **Create Adjustment** → `adjustment_id` · **Trigger SOS** → `sos_incident_id` · **Report Lost Item** → `lost_item_id` · **Create Shift (Rota)** → `shift_id` · **Add Availability Plan** → `availability_plan_id` · **Submit Maintenance Record** / **Maintenance Records Queue** → `maintenance_record_id` · **List All Stations** (admin EV) → `ev_station_id` · **Reserve EV Stall** → `ev_reservation_id` · **List Fleet Agreements** → `fleet_agreement_id` · **Get Fleet Agreement** → `remittance_id` · **Ledger Transactions** → `ledger_entry_id`. The admin *Create* requests (city, vehicle class, pricing, surge rule…) overwrite the matching id with the new record — re-run the two list requests above to switch back to the seeded data.

Every variable is declared on the collection, so nothing resolves to an undefined `{{...}}`. All ids are UUIDs.

### 8. Sessions

Admin dashboard tokens expire after `SANCTUM_TOKEN_EXPIRATION` minutes (default 480 = 8 h). Passenger and driver app tokens expire after `SANCTUM_APP_TOKEN_EXPIRATION` minutes (default 43,200 = 30 days). An expired token returns `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`.

---

## What Changed for the Apps (October 2026)
See `doc/technical/FRONTEND_UPDATE_PAYMENTS_EV_SURGE.md` for the payouts, tips, EV, fuel type and surge changes per app, breaking ones first. Lost & Found (Phase 2): `doc/technical/FRONTEND_UPDATE_LOST_AND_FOUND.md`. Advanced disputes (Phase 2): `doc/technical/FRONTEND_UPDATE_ADVANCED_DISPUTES.md`. Driver scheduling and vehicle maintenance (Phase 2): `doc/technical/FRONTEND_UPDATE_DRIVER_SCHEDULING_MAINTENANCE.md`. Offline trip flags (appeals, verified cash-taking, deactivation reason and record, 48-hour driver response window, route map): `doc/technical/FRONTEND_UPDATE_OFFLINE_FLAGS_DESIGN_GAPS.md` (admin) and `doc/technical/MOBILE_UPDATE_OFFLINE_FLAGS.md` (driver app; passenger app unchanged).

## Content Type
- JSON: `Content-Type: application/json`
- File uploads: `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`

## Error Format
All errors return `{ "message": "...", "error_code": "..." }`. Validation errors (422) include an `errors` object with field-level details.

| Status | `error_code` | When |
|--------|--------------|------|
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Missing, invalid or expired token |
| 403 | `HTTP_ERROR` | Wrong user type or admin role |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | `Resource not found.` (bad id) or `The requested endpoint does not exist.` (bad URL) |
| 409 | `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` | The ride/SOS changed state concurrently (body includes `current_status`) |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Field validation failed (`errors` object) |
| 422 | `INVALID_PARAMETER` | A malformed id or date reached the database |
| 429 | `HTTP_ERROR` | Rate limited — honour the `Retry-After` header |
| 500 | `SERVER_ERROR` | Unexpected error (details only when debugging is enabled) |

request.description:
Returns app configuration including minimum version requirements for force-update enforcement. No authentication required.

`scheduled_rides` gives the booking screen its limits for scheduled rides: offer pickup times from `min_lead_minutes` after now up to `max_advance_days` ahead; hide the option when `enabled` is false. `reservation_fee` and `late_cancellation_fee` (NGN, 0 = off) and `late_cancellation_window_minutes` let the app explain fees; `driver_reservations_enabled` tells the driver app whether to show the reservations screen.

`third_party_bookings` drives "Book for someone else": offer `payment_methods`, and for "Who gets the PIN?" show `share_with_options` (each has `value`, `label` and `description`; show the label and description as given, they are worded from the current tracking setting) with `default_share_with` pre-selected, and send the chosen `value` as `share_with` on the booking. Hide the question when `share_with_options` is empty.

`payments`: `methods` lists how passengers may pay (`card`, `wallet`, and `cash` only while `cash_enabled`). Cash is off by default; hide it when `cash_enabled` is false.

request.description:
No auth required. Detects the live city for the given coordinates.

**Detection flow:**
1. Boundary matching decides, exactly as for estimates and bookings (any launch status for the 404 below):
   - Point: haversine distance <= radius_km
   - Polygon: ray-casting point-in-polygon
2. Only when no boundary holds the point is the reverse-geocoded city name matched against cities that have **no boundary drawn yet**. A district name from the geocoder (e.g. "Ikeja") never overrides a boundary.
3. `resolved_address` is the reverse-geocoded address, for display.

Boundaries cannot overlap (saving refuses it), so a point belongs to one city. If legacy boundaries do overlap, the smallest city wins, for detection and booking alike.

Returns 404 if no live city matches. Inside a city that is onboarding or paused, the 404 adds `unavailable_city` so the app can offer the waitlist.

request.description: Public endpoint (no auth, 60/min). The data behind trip sharing and the no-app tracking page sent to third-party riders (`GET /track/{ride}/{token}` on the API host renders it). Returns the status, pickup/destination, the driver's first name, photo and car (make, model, colour, plate), the driver's live position and ETA while the ride is active, the emergency number and the E-tiGo safety line. For a third-party ride also `rider_first_name` and `booked_by_first_name`. Nothing about the passenger's account. Expires 1 hour after the ride ends (410).

item.name: Authentication

request.description:
Sends a 6-digit OTP through Sendchamp: WhatsApp (approved OTP template) first, SMS fallback. The SMS reads "Your E-tiGo verification code is 482910. It expires in 5 minutes. Do not share it with anyone." 60-second cooldown between requests. Code expires after 5 minutes.

If neither channel accepts the code (production only), the response is `429` "Failed to send verification code. Please try again." and the code is cancelled.

**Non-production:** OTP is always `123456` and message delivery is skipped. Use this code in Verify OTP.

response.name: 200 — OTP Sent
429 — Cooldown Active
429 — Delivery Failed

request.description:
Returns the OAuth redirect URL for the given provider. The mobile app opens this URL in a system browser (not a WebView). After the user authorizes, the backend redirects to the app deep link: `etigo-{type}:///auth/callback?code=...&state=...`.

The app then calls `POST /auth/social/exchange` with the received `code` to get the session token.

**Parameters:**
- `provider` — One of: `google`, `apple`, `facebook`
- `type` — Must be `passenger` or `driver`. Determines the deep link scheme for the callback.
- `state` — A random CSRF-protection string (min 16 characters) that the app generates and verifies on callback.

No auth required. Rate-limited to 5 requests/minute.

response.name: 200 — Redirect URL
422 — Invalid Provider

request.description:
Exchange a one-time authorization code (received via deep link callback after social OAuth) for a session token. The code is single-use and expires after 5 minutes.

**Deep Link Flow:**
1. App calls `POST /auth/social/redirect` with `provider`, `type`, and a random `state`
2. App opens the returned `redirect_url` in a browser
3. User completes OAuth with the provider
4. Backend redirects to the app deep link: `etigo-{type}:///auth/callback?code=...&state=...`
5. App calls this endpoint with the `code` to get the session token

request.description:
Passenger token. Returns a quote for every active vehicle class in the pickup's city.

- Distance and duration come from the maps provider (Google, then Mapbox, then a straight-line estimate).
- `fare_estimate` already includes the current surge and the passenger's loyalty-tier discount; the discount is also returned as `booking_fee_discount` (NGN).
- Booking (`POST /rides`) and the final fare use the same calculation. The quote is an upfront fare: it changes only for a waiting charge or a trip that runs significantly longer than the quoted time.
- Cross-city or very long trips return a `warnings` array. A pickup in a city that is not open, and identical pickup/destination, return 422.

**The pickup decides the city (24 Oct 2026):** the server books and quotes the city whose drawn boundary holds the pickup. `city_id` is optional: it is only used for a pickup outside every drawn city (or one inside the city sent, e.g. on a shared border), and a stale or wrong `city_id` is corrected rather than refused. A pickup inside a city that is onboarding or paused returns 422 on `pickup_lat` with that city's message (on `city_id` when the city used is the one you sent). A pickup outside every city with no `city_id` returns 422 on `pickup_lat`: "E-tiGo is not available at this pickup location yet."

The response's `city` (`id`, `name`) is the city quoted; show it as the trip's city.

request.description:
Passenger books a ride. Uses `{{economy_class_id}}` (run **List City Vehicle Classes** first). `city_id` is optional: the pickup decides the city. **Sets `{{ride_id}}` and `{{share_token}}`.**

- Returns the ride (`reference_number` e.g. `TRP-NG-000123`) and the 4-digit `pin_code` for the driver.
- One active ride per passenger: a second booking returns 409.
- `payment_method`: `card` (saved default card, or a payment link), `wallet` (a hold for the estimate is placed now) or `bank_transfer`; `cash` only while cash payments are on.
- The surge multiplier and tier discount in effect now are locked in for the final fare.
- Optional `promo_code`: validated now against city, class, fare, time window, tier and usage limits — an invalid code rejects the booking with 422; the discount is applied at completion.
- To book for later, add `scheduled_pickup_at` — see **Book Scheduled Ride**. Ride responses carry `is_scheduled`, `scheduled_pickup_at` and `scheduled` (null for rides booked for now).
- While the passenger owes a balance (unpaid late-cancellation fee or wallet fare), booking returns 422 `BALANCE_DUE` with `balance_due`; pay it with **Passenger › Balance Due › Pay Balance Due**.

**The pickup decides the city (24 Oct 2026):** the server books and quotes the city whose drawn boundary holds the pickup. `city_id` is optional: it is only used for a pickup outside every drawn city (or one inside the city sent, e.g. on a shared border), and a stale or wrong `city_id` is corrected rather than refused. A pickup inside a city that is onboarding or paused returns 422 on `pickup_lat` with that city's message (on `city_id` when the city used is the one you sent). A pickup outside every city with no `city_id` returns 422 on `pickup_lat`: "E-tiGo is not available at this pickup location yet." The ride's `city` is the city booked.

**Cash is off (24 Oct 2026):** `payment_method: cash` returns 422 on `payment_method` ("Cash isn't accepted. Pay by card or from your wallet.") unless Finance switches on the wallet setting `cash_payments_enabled`. Offer the methods in `payments.methods` from **App Configuration**.

request.description:
Book and pay for a ride someone else takes (Phase 2, BE2-3P). Same body as **Create Ride** plus `rider_name`, `rider_phone` and `rider_age_confirmed: true` (the rider is 18+ or an adult travels with them). **Sets `{{ride_id}}` and `{{share_token}}`.**

- You (the booker) stay the ride's passenger: you pay, cancel, rate and see the trip in your history.
- `rider_phone`: E.164, or a Nigerian local number (`0802 000 0002`), stored as `+2348020000002`. Your own number makes it a normal ride.
- Payment: `wallet` or `card` only by default; `cash` and `bank_transfer` return 422 unless operations allow them.
- Does not count as your own active ride (you can ride yourself at the same time). Limits: 2 active third-party rides; 10 different rider numbers per 24 hours (cancelled bookings count).
- `share_with` ("Who gets the PIN?"): `rider` ("Rider only") or `both` ("Both of us"). It decides only who gets the PIN; live tracking follows the operations setting (`tracking_recipient`, default `both`, so you keep following the trip and the rider gets a tracking link). Omit it to use the admin default (`third_party_bookings.default_share_with` in **App Configuration**); ignored when `share_with_options` is empty. Any other value returns 422. What applied is saved on the ride (`third_party.pin_recipient`, `tracking_recipient`). When a driver is assigned the rider gets a WhatsApp message (SMS fallback) with the driver, car, plate, PIN and a no-app tracking link (`/track/{ride}/{token}`).
- `pin_code` is null with `share_with: rider` (or a rider-only admin default). If the rider's message fails, `rider_notification_status` becomes `failed` and the PIN is shown to you whatever the policy.
- `third_party.rider_notification_status` is `null` when the policy sends the rider nothing (booker-only PIN and tracking). Links in the addresses you type are removed from the rider's message.
- We never tell you whether the number has an E-tiGo account.

request.description:
Books a ride for later: `POST /rides` plus `scheduled_pickup_at` (ISO 8601 **with a UTC offset**). **Sets `{{scheduled_ride_id}}`.** Change the time in the body to one 30 minutes to 3 days from now before sending.

- The ride is created in `scheduled` status: no PIN (`pin_code` is `null`), no wallet hold, no matching yet. Matching starts `scheduled.dispatch_at` (15 min before pickup); the PIN appears on the ride then.
- The fare is quoted and locked now, with the surge in effect **at the pickup time** (time-based/manual rules; never demand surge). A promo code must be valid at the pickup time.
- Wallet bookings: the balance must cover the quote now; it is held at dispatch.
- Limits (operations-editable, see `GET /config` → `scheduled_rides`): 30 min to 3 days ahead, 3 upcoming bookings, 30 min apart.
- Booking for later works while the passenger is on another ride.

request.description: A scheduled booking (`scheduled_pickup_at`) for someone else. The rider gets a WhatsApp/SMS reminder with the booking details (no PIN) at the scheduled-ride reminder time (60 min before pickup by default); a booking already inside that window, or an edit with no reminder still to come, is sent to the rider at once. The driver details, PIN and tracking link follow when a driver is on the way. Bookings only clash (`min_minutes_between_bookings`) when they are for the same person, and dispatch is not held up by your own ride. Editing the booking to `cash`/`bank_transfer` is refused like at booking. **Sets `{{ride_id}}`.** `share_with` works as on **Book Ride for Someone Else** and is kept until dispatch.

request.description:
Changes a booking before `scheduled.dispatch_at`. Send only what changes: `scheduled_pickup_at`, a new pickup (`pickup_lat`, `pickup_lng`, `pickup_address` together), a new destination (`destination_*` together) or `payment_method`. The fare is quoted again and any promo re-checked.

422 `errors.ride` once dispatch is near; `errors.scheduled_pickup_at` for the same limits as booking.

Changing `scheduled_pickup_at` or the pickup releases a driver who reserved the booking; a new destination or payment method keeps them.

A new pickup must stay in the booking's city (its prices and drivers were fixed at booking): a pickup inside another city's boundary returns 422 on `pickup_lat` — "This pickup is in Abuja, not the booking's city. Cancel and book again to be picked up there.", or that city's not-open message.

Changing `payment_method` to `cash` is refused (422) while cash payments are off, as for booking.

response.name: 422 — Too Close to Dispatch

request.description: Cancels a booking before it is dispatched. Optional `reason` / `reason_details`. Free unless a driver has reserved the booking **and** the ride is less than 30 minutes away; then the passenger pays the city's **economy base fare** (client decision), paid to the reserved driver. `emergency`, `safety_concern`, `vehicle_mismatch` and `driver_no_show` are never charged. Show `scheduled.cancellation_fee_if_cancelled_now` before confirming. Wallet and card bookings are charged at once; cash and bank-transfer bookings (or a short wallet or declined card) get a balance due (`late_cancellation_fee_status: balance_due`). Once dispatched, use **Cancel Ride**.

item.name: Create Ride — Stale city_id / Pickup in a City Not Open

request.description:
`city_id` names Lagos but the pickup is in Abuja. The server books the city the pickup lies in, so:

- Abuja **live**: the ride is created in Abuja (201, `ride.city.name` = Abuja). The stale `city_id` is not an error.
- Abuja **onboarding or paused**: 422 on `pickup_lat` with Abuja's not-open message, so a city that has not opened cannot be booked under a live city's name and prices.

response.name: 422 — City Not Open

request.description:
Polling fallback when the WebSocket drops. Ride passenger, assigned driver or admin.

- Active ride: the driver's latest position (`lat`, `lng`, `heading`, `speed`, `timestamp`) and a throttled `eta` (to pickup before the trip, to the destination during it).
- Ride completed or cancelled: `location` is `null` with "Live location is only available during an active ride." — admins still get the last position.
- No recent position: `"Driver location unavailable."`

Prefer the `private-ride.{rideId}` channel for real-time updates.

request.description:
Passenger tips once per completed ride (between the tip settings' min and max). `source` says how the tip is paid: `wallet`, `card` or `cash`, defaulting to the ride's payment method; the response's `payment.tip_method` records it.

- Card: charged to the default saved card first. A decline records nothing (422 "Failed to charge tip amount.") and the passenger can retry. If the bank does not answer, the tip stays reserved and is checked by its reference before anything is charged again (422 "We could not confirm your tip payment with the bank yet. Please try again in a few minutes; you will not be charged twice."); a later attempt settles it first ("Your earlier tip went through, so you were not charged again."). Credited to the driver in full.
- Wallet: paid from the passenger's wallet balance and credited to the driver in full. Balance too low → 422 "Your wallet balance is too low for this tip."; frozen or closed wallet → 422 "Wallet is frozen or closed."
- Cash: recorded only; the driver collects it in person. Only on cash rides (422 "Cash tips can only be recorded on cash rides.").
- Bank-transfer rides must send `source` (`wallet` or `card`): 422 "Choose how to pay the tip: wallet or card." otherwise.

A second tip → 422.

request.description:
Returns a detailed receipt for a completed ride including fare breakdown, vehicle details, card info, tip, tier discount, promo discount, carbon emissions, and payment details. Accessible by the ride's passenger, driver, or any admin.

**`payment` totals** — exactly one is present:
- `total_charged` (number) — when `status` is `captured`, `collected` or `settled`; fare + tip actually charged.
- `amount_due` (string) — any other status (e.g. `pending`, `pending_collection` for cash not yet collected, `failed`); the fare still owed, without the tip.

`payment` is `null` when the ride has no payment record.

**`trip_time`** — fares are upfront. `duration_minutes` is the time billed; `trip_time` shows `quoted_minutes`, `actual_minutes` (trip start to completion, may be `null`), `billed_minutes` and `adjusted`. The quoted time is billed unless the trip ran more than 25% (and at least 10 minutes) longer; then the actual time is billed, capped at 3× the quote, and `adjusted` is `true` — show the passenger a note. `null` for rides completed before upfront fares.

**Errors:** 403 — not the ride's passenger or driver, and not an admin. 404 — the ride is not completed.

request.description:
File a dispute / report an issue for a completed ride. Both passengers and drivers can file disputes. Supports optional evidence photo uploads (up to 5 images, max 5MB each) and an optional audio recording (mp3, m4a, wav, ogg, webm, aac, max 10MB).

**Content-Type:** `multipart/form-data` (when uploading photos) or `application/json`

**Categories:** `safety_concern`, `driver_behaviour`, `route_deviation`, `fare_dispute`, `vehicle_condition`, `item_left_behind`, `payment_issue`, `other`

**Category Labels:**
- `safety_concern` → Safety concern
- `driver_behaviour` → Driver behaviour
- `route_deviation` → Wrong route taken
- `fare_dispute` → Fare is incorrect
- `vehicle_condition` → Vehicle condition
- `item_left_behind` → Lost item
- `payment_issue` → Payment issue
- `other` → Something else

**Validation:**
- Ride must be completed — or, for the passenger only, a cancelled scheduled booking they were charged (or owe) a late-cancellation fee for (SR-4); see **File Dispute — Late-Cancellation Fee**
- User must be a participant
- Cannot file more than one dispute per ride per user
- Description: 10–2000 characters
- Photos: max 5, each max 5MB, jpg/jpeg/png/webp only
- Audio: max 1, max 10MB, mp3/m4a/wav/ogg/webm/aac only

**Phase 2:** a new dispute goes to support tier 1; a `safety_concern` goes straight to the Safety team (message: "Report received. Our safety team has been alerted and will contact you shortly."). The response now includes `evidence`, `stage`, `stage_label`, `can_add_evidence` and `appeal`.

item.name: 🔐 Driver — KYC Verification
item.description:
KYC identity verification endpoints for drivers. Uses QoreID for NIN, Driver's License, Vehicle Plate, and Liveness verification.

**Required verifications for `verified` status:** NIN + Driver's License + Vehicle Plate.

**Test values (FakeKycGateway):**
- IDs starting with `000` → fail
- All other IDs → pass
- Liveness sessions with `fail` in session ID → fail

**Response:** `200` with `{kyc_status, kyc_verified_at, verifications}`

request.description:
**Auth required (driver).**

Submits a NIN for verification against QoreID. Name matching is performed against the driver's registered name.

**Required fields:**
- `nin_number` — string, exactly 11 digits

**Responses:**
- `200` — NIN verified successfully
- `422` — Verification failed (name mismatch, invalid NIN)
- `409` — Already verified or in progress

**Test:** Use `00012345678` to trigger a failure.

request.description:
Toggle driver online/offline status. Requires approved status, registered vehicle with assigned class. Returns reasons array on failure.

An online driver whose app sends no location for 5 minutes gets a `driver_location_missing` push (`MATCHING_SILENT_DRIVER_WARNING_MINUTES`); after 30 minutes (`MATCHING_SILENT_DRIVER_OFFLINE_MINUTES`) they are set offline and get a `driver_set_offline` push. A driver on a trip is only warned, never set offline.

**Multi-city:** refused (422, in `reasons`) while the driver's city is still onboarding. In a paused city the driver can go online for bookings made before the pause, and the response has a `city_notice`.

**Phase 2 (OQ-19/20):** plug-in cars may send `battery_level_percent` (0–100). Refused (422 `reasons`) when the car's insurance, roadworthiness or vehicle licence expired more than 7 days ago, and for a shared fleet car outside the driver's shift window or while the previous driver still has the car. A shared car passes to the shift driver here. A 200 adds `shift` (shared cars) and `vehicle_notice` (papers expiring or in their grace period).

request.description:
Update driver's real-time GPS location. Rate-limited to 1 request/second per driver. Stores coordinates in Redis geo set and broadcasts a `driver.location.updated` event via WebSocket to ride participants and admin dashboard. Returns throttled ETA when the driver has an active ride.

**Requires:** Online, approved driver with valid Sanctum token.

**Validation:**
- `lat` (required): Latitude between -90 and 90
- `lng` (required): Longitude between -180 and 180
- `heading` (optional): Bearing 0–360 degrees
- `speed` (optional): Speed in km/h, >= 0
- `timestamp` (optional): a date/time; accepted but not used — the server's time is recorded

**Rate Limit:** 429 if called more than once per second.

Locations stop counting 2 minutes after the last one. After 5 minutes without one the driver gets a `driver_location_missing` push, and after 30 minutes the server sets them offline (never during a trip). The app must keep sending locations whenever the driver is online, including in the background (Android foreground service, iOS background location) and after it is reopened.

`accuracy` (optional, metres): the phone's horizontal GPS accuracy; shown to compliance reviewers on anti-offline flags.

item.description: Driver-side ride lifecycle actions: accepting/rejecting dispatched ride requests, arriving at pickup, verifying passenger PIN, and completing rides.

request.description:
Driver accepts the ride they were offered (the matching engine offers one ride to one driver at a time; an unanswered offer expires after 20 s). The ride moves `searching` → `matched` → `driver_en_route`. The ride and the driver are locked, so the first acceptance wins and a driver can never hold two rides.

- 403 — the ride was not offered to this driver, or the driver's earnings balance is below the allowed negative threshold.
- 409 — another driver already accepted, or the driver already has an active ride.
- 422 — the ride is no longer open for acceptance.

item.description: Phase 2 driver scheduling (OQ-20). Availability plans are for every driver and voluntary: they never stop a driver going online and passengers never see them. Shifts exist only for E-tiGo fleet cars in **shift mode** (shared by two or more drivers). A shift driver can go online from 15 min before the start (`online_from`); new offers stop 15 min before the end (`offers_stop_at`); not online 30 min after the start → `missed` (operations emailed, no fine; can still start late). The car passes to the shift driver when they go online in their window, once the previous driver is offline and not on a trip. All times are settings (`/admin/settings/driver-scheduling`).

request.description:
Driver reserves a charging stall. **Electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles only**: the vehicle's `fuel_type` must be `electric` or `plug_in_hybrid` (`can_charge: true` on the vehicle), otherwise 422. Three outcomes:

1. **reserved** (201) — a stall was free and is locked for 30 minutes (`EV_RESERVATION_EXPIRY`); not activated by then, it expires and goes to the next driver in the queue.
2. **queued** (200) — all stalls busy but one frees up within 15 minutes; the driver is notified when it is theirs.
3. **retry** (200) — no stall soon; try again after `retry_after_minutes`.

**Reservation fee** (₦500, `EV_RESERVATION_FEE`; waived for Platinum and Diamond drivers, `fee_waived: true`). It is taken from the driver's available earnings when a stall is actually held for them: at once for `reserved`, on promotion for `queued`. `fee_charged_at` shows when. Like cash-ride commission, it may take the balance below zero down to the wallet's `max_negative_balance`; beyond that → 422 "Your earnings balance cannot cover the ₦500.00 reservation fee." (also checked before queueing). A driver whose earnings account is frozen → 422 "Your earnings account is on hold, so the reservation fee cannot be paid. Contact support." A queued driver who can no longer pay when a stall frees up is cancelled (reason in `notes`), gets an `ev_reservation_cancelled` push, and the stall goes to the next driver. Refunded on cancellation within 2 minutes of being charged (`EV_RESERVATION_FREE_CANCEL_MINUTES`); kept after that and on a no-show. `free_cancellation_until` gives the deadline for a countdown (null when there is nothing to refund).

One open reservation per driver (422). **Sets `{{ev_reservation_id}}`.**

item.name: Driver — Vehicle Maintenance
item.description: Phase 2 vehicle maintenance (OQ-19). Every car: routine service (5,000 km or 3 months), tyres & brakes (6 months), insurance, roadworthiness certificate, vehicle licence. Electric and plug-in hybrid cars also: battery health (12 months) and charge level. Overdue maintenance only warns. **Insurance, roadworthiness or vehicle licence expired more than 7 days ago keeps the car off the road** (no going online, no offers) until a renewed paper is approved; a trip in progress is never ended. Drivers of their own car submit records with proof; fleet cars are recorded by operations. Upload papers with **Driver — Onboarding › Upload Document** (`roadworthiness_certificate` and `vehicle_licence` need `expires_at`).

request.description:
Resolves the account with Paystack and saves it as the driver's primary payout account.

Every save needs `otp_code`, the first account included: call **Request Bank Account Code** first (non-production code: `123456`). Without it → 422 `errors.otp_code`; a wrong or expired code → 422 `errors.otp_code` with the reason.

Paystack resolves the account before the code is checked, so a resolve failure does not use up the code. Each save notifies the driver (`payout_account_changed`, in-app and push) and sends a WhatsApp/SMS alert regardless of preferences.

Payout safeguards: the response has `payout_eligibility` (`can_request_payouts`, `code`, `message`, `payouts_held_until`). A replacement account is held for the `payout_account_hold_hours` wallet setting (default 24); a name mismatch is saved for finance review (default) or refused in `block` mode (422 `code: payout_account_name_mismatch`, code not used up). **Sets `{{payout_account_id}}`.**

response.name: 200 — Payouts

request.description:
Driver requests a withdrawal (kobo, at least the `min_payout` wallet setting, default 100000 = ₦1,000) to their verified bank account. **Sets `{{payout_id}}`.**

Lifecycle: `requested` → `approved` (finance) → `processing` (transfer sent) → `paid`, or `rejected` / `failed` / `reversed`. The money leaves the available balance when the transfer is sent; a failed or reversed transfer returns it. If Paystack cannot be reached, answers with a server error or never confirms, the payout stays `approved` or `processing` with the money reserved until Paystack's answer is known (checked automatically every 15 minutes); it is never lost or paid twice. One open payout at a time (422), rate limit 3/min. Blocked by a payout safeguard on the bank account → 422 with `code` (`payout_account_on_hold`, `payout_account_under_review`, `payout_account_rejected`) and `payouts_held_until`.

item.description: Endpoints for authenticated driver users. Covers onboarding, KYC verification, vehicle management, and ride operations.

item.name: Admin
Admin — Overview
item.description:
**Required Role(s):** any admin for **Get Overview** and **Global Search**; Operations for **Live Operations Panel** (Super Admin always has access).

The console's landing page. Each card or search group is `null` when the admin's role cannot open the screen behind it, so hide it rather than show zero. The greeting uses `first_name` from **Auth — Admin → Get Admin Profile**; the bell uses **Notifications → Unread Count**.

- `change_pct` on active rides and drivers online compares with a snapshot from this time yesterday (taken every 5 minutes); `null` until a day of snapshots exists after release.
- Revenue is gross fares of rides completed since midnight Lagos time, against the same stretch of yesterday.
- Poll every 30–60 s; for live ride movement use the `admin.rides` WebSocket.

request.description:
Headline cards (`stats`), the "Needs your attention" row (`attention`) and `recent_activity`.

- `stats.active_rides` / `drivers_online`: `count`, `change_pct` vs this time yesterday (`null` when no snapshot), `compared_at`. Drivers add `on_trip` and `utilisation_pct`.
- `stats.open_disputes`: `count`, `overdue` (missed their next target).
- `stats.revenue`: `amount` (gross fares, NGN), `completed_rides`, `change_pct`, `previous_amount`; `period` = `today`, `timezone` = `Africa/Lagos`.
- `attention`: `safety_alerts` (`count`, `critical` = not yet picked up), `compliance_reviews` (`count`, `high_severity` = level 3), `pending_kyc`, `unmatched_requests`.
- `recent_activity[]`: `event`, `category` (icon), `title`, `subtitle`, `subject` (`type`, `id`, `reference_number`) to open the detail page, `actor` (`null` for system), `created_at`. Only areas your role can open; per-trip events like ride completed are not listed.
- `can_view_live_operations`: show the Live operations panel.

response.name: 200 — Overview (Super Admin)

query.description: City UUID (default: city with most active rides)

request.description:
Map pins and latest trips for one city. Operations only.

- `cities`: cities with active rides, busiest first, for the switcher.
- `markers` (max 300, newest first; `markers_truncated` when more): `lat`/`lng` from the driver's live location (`position_source: driver`) or the pickup (`pickup`); `needs_attention` = red pin.
- `rides[]`: `reference_number`, `status_label`, `pickup_address`, `destination_address`, `passenger.name`, `driver.name`, `attention_reasons` (`sos`, `driver_location_missing`).
- `summary`: `active_rides` (full count), `needs_attention` (among markers).
- `city` is `null` with empty lists when nothing is moving and no `city_id` was given.

request.description:

item.description: Operations. Shared fleet cars on a shift timetable, and the coverage of drivers' voluntary availability plans (OQ-20). Shifts exist only for E-tiGo fleet cars in **shift mode** (shared by two or more drivers). A shift driver can go online from 15 min before the start (`online_from`); new offers stop 15 min before the end (`offers_stop_at`); not online 30 min after the start → `missed` (operations emailed, no fine; can still start late). The car passes to the shift driver when they go online in their window, once the previous driver is offline and not on a trip. All times are settings (`/admin/settings/driver-scheduling`).

item.name: Turn Shift Mode On for a Fleet Car

request.description: `shift_mode: true` lets drivers share the car on shifts. Fleet cars only, and not on an active hire-purchase agreement (a shift-mode car cannot go on hire purchase either). `false` is refused while the car has upcoming shifts. Operations only.

request.description:
Returns paginated cities with aggregate counts.

**Query params:**
- `is_active` (bool) — filter by active/inactive status (active = live)
- `launch_status` (string) — comma list of `onboarding`, `live`, `paused`
- `search` (string) — filter by city name (partial match)
- `state` (string) — filter by Nigerian state (e.g. `Lagos`)
- `region` (string) — filter by geopolitical zone (e.g. `South-West`)
- `per_page` (int) — results per page (default: 20, max: 100)

Each city includes `vehicle_classes_count` and `drivers_count` for the list view.

Filter `launch_status` (comma list). Each city has `launch_status`, `launch_date`, `launched_at`, `paused_at`, `pause_reason` and `waitlist_count` (passengers still waiting).

**Overlapping boundaries:** each city has `overlapping_cities` (`[{id, name}]`, empty when none): cities whose boundary overlaps it, saved before overlaps were refused. Show a warning badge; the fix is to redraw one boundary (**Update City**).

request.description:
Creates a new city/service area.

**Required fields:** name, state
**Optional fields:** boundary, vehicle_class_ids, timezone, currency_code, launch_date

**Auto-derived by backend:**
- region — derived from state (e.g. Lagos → South-West)
- slug — generated from name, auto-suffixed if duplicate
- area_sq_km — calculated from Polygon boundary coordinates
- is_active — false: a new city starts with `launch_status` `onboarding` (is_active is true only when live)
- timezone — defaults to Africa/Lagos if not sent
- currency_code — defaults to NGN if not sent

**Boundary types:**
- Point + radius_km: circular service area (simpler setup)
- Polygon: custom shape with coordinates array (admin draws on map)

**State validation:** must be one of the 36 Nigerian states or FCT. Use GET /lookup/states to populate the dropdown.

**Vehicle classes:** pass an array of UUIDs from GET /admin/vehicle-classes. They are synced (replaces any existing associations).

**Multi-city:** `launch_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, nullable) is the client's target launch date, a readiness gate. A new city starts in `onboarding`. A `boundary` that overlaps another city returns 422 on `boundary` (shared borders are fine). `timezone` must be Africa/Lagos and `currency_code` NGN.

422 — Validation Error
422 — Boundary Overlaps

request.description:
For the map editor: checks a boundary before saving it. Saves nothing.

- `can_save` is false when the boundary overlaps another city (create/update would return 422 on `boundary`); `overlapping_city` names it.
- `area_sq_km` and `centre` describe the shape.
- `warnings` flags a boundary that saves but is probably wrong: coordinates swapped (GeoJSON is [lng, lat]) or outside Nigeria, a circle instead of an outline, under 10 km² or over 2,500 km², an outline crossing itself, or more than 250 km from the capital of `state`.

Optional `state` (checks the boundary is drawn there) and `city_id` (the city being edited, whose own boundary is not an overlap).

request.description:
Returns city with loaded vehicle classes and aggregate counts.

**Counts included:**
- `vehicle_classes_count` — number of assigned vehicle classes
- `drivers_count` — total registered drivers in this city
- `trips_count` — total rides (all statuses)
- `active_rides_count` — rides currently in progress (Matched, DriverEnRoute, DriverArrived, InProgress)
- `active_drivers_count` — approved drivers currently online

**Multi-city:** the response adds `readiness` ({ready, missing, counts}); the full checklist is `GET /admin/cities/{city}/readiness`.

`warnings` (plain English, never blocking) flags pricing gaps and a boundary that overlaps another city: "Oshodi's boundary overlaps Lagos. Pickups in the overlap are booked in the smaller of the two cities. Redraw one boundary so they only share a border."

`warnings` also flags a doubtful boundary (coordinates swapped or outside Nigeria, a circle, under 10 km² or over 2,500 km², crossing itself, far from the city's state) and a live city with no boundary. See **Check City Boundary**.

request.description:
Move a city: onboarding → live (first launch; every required readiness gate must pass, else 422 with `readiness`), live → paused (`reason` required), paused → live (resume; no checklist), paused → onboarding.

Pausing never touches trips in progress. `scheduled_rides` (pause only): `honour` (bookings still go ahead) or `cancel` (each upcoming booking is cancelled with reason `city_paused` and the passenger is told); default from the `pause_scheduled_rides` setting. Back to onboarding always cancels upcoming bookings. Going live notifies the waitlist; drivers in the city hear about launches and pauses (`city_status_changed`). item.name: Admin — Manual Assignment
item.description:
**Required Role(s):** Operations (Super Admin always has access)

Manual assignment of drivers to rides that automatic matching did not place (support escalations, `no_driver_found`).

### Flow
1. **List Pending Rides** — saves the first ride as `{{ride_id}}`.
2. **Available Drivers for Ride** — saves the nearest driver's user id as `{{driver_user_id}}`.
3. **Manually Assign Driver** — assigns `{{driver_user_id}}` to `{{ride_id}}`.

### Assignment is instant
There is no request for the driver to accept or decline. The ride goes straight to `matched` → `driver_en_route`, the driver and passenger are notified, and admins get `ride.status.updated`. So there is no answer timeout and nothing to cancel while waiting; to undo an assignment the ride is cancelled as usual.

### How "available" is decided
Online and approved · reported GPS in the last 2 minutes · not on a trip (`matched`, `driver_en_route`, `driver_arrived`, `in_progress`) · in the ride's city · vehicle in the ride's class · within `radius_km` (default 5 km) of the pickup · nearest first.

### Keeping the list current (WebSocket)
Private channel `admin.rides`, event `ride.status.updated` (`ride_id, passenger_id, driver_id, previous_status, status, actor_type, actor_id, occurred_at`):
- **new pending ride** → `status` = `searching` (from `requested`)
- **no driver found** → `status` = `no_driver_found`
- **ride matched** → `status` = `matched` / `driver_en_route` (`actor_type` = `admin` for a manual assignment)
- **ride cancelled** → `status` = `cancelled`

See **Real-Time (WebSocket) → Authorize Channel — Admin** for subscribing.

### Common errors
`401 UNAUTHENTICATED` · `403` insufficient admin role · `404 NOT_FOUND` unknown ride · `422 INVALID_PARAMETER` a malformed UUID filter.

### Test data on staging
`php artisan db:seed --class=MonitoringDemoSeeder` seeds 3 pending rides in Lagos (2 `searching`, 1 `no_driver_found`) with online demo drivers 0.8–6.5 km from their pickups, plus active rides at every stage. Demo drivers report their location every minute via the scheduler, each has rated past trips, and they are never offered rides by automatic matching (manual assignment only). Re-run the seeder to reset rides used up by testing.

query.description: Comma-separated: requested, searching, no_driver_found, matched, driver_en_route. Omit for unassigned rides only. Admin-assigned rides are driver_en_route, so include it for a "Matched" tab.
Partial, case-insensitive: trip reference, passenger name, city name or vehicle class name

request.description:
Rides waiting for a driver — `requested`, `searching` or `no_driver_found` with no driver — **oldest first**. `no_driver_found` rides drop off 24 hours after they were requested. Pass `status` to include matched rides (`matched`, `driver_en_route`).

**Matched rows** also carry `driver` (name, phone), `driver_rating`, `driver_vehicle` (`make`, `model`, `colour`, `plate_number`) and `matched_at` (when the driver accepted or the admin assigned).

**`summary`** (follows `city_id` and the 24-hour window only):
- `awaiting_driver` — unassigned `requested` + `searching` + `no_driver_found`. Use it for the **"needs attention" badge** on the Rides tab.
- `by_status` — counts for each status the list can show.

Saves the first ride's id as `{{ride_id}}`.

query.description: Search radius from the pickup in km (default 5)

request.description:
Drivers who can take `{{ride_id}}`, **nearest first**.

Eligible = online and approved, GPS reported in the last 2 minutes, not on a trip, in the ride's city, vehicle in the ride's class, within `radius_km` of the pickup.

Per driver: `name`, `phone`, `rating` (null when unrated), `vehicle` (`make`, `model`, `plate_number`, `colour`, `vehicle_class`), `location` (with `updated_at`), `distance_km` (straight line to pickup) and `eta_minutes` (that distance at 30 km/h).

Saves the nearest driver's **user id** as `{{driver_user_id}}` — the id **Manually Assign Driver** expects.

request.description:
Assigns `{{driver_user_id}}` (a driver's **user** id — `user_id` from Available Drivers) to `{{ride_id}}`. **Instant**: the ride goes straight to `driver_en_route`; there is no accept/decline step.

The ride must be `requested`, `searching` or `no_driver_found`. For `no_driver_found`, it is refused if the passenger has booked again since, and a wallet ride's fare hold is placed again.

**Errors**
| Status | `error_code` | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | `errors.driver_id`: required / not a UUID / unknown user, `No driver profile found for this user.`, `Driver must be approved.`, `Driver must be online.`, `Driver vehicle class does not match the ride request.`, `Driver already has an active ride.` |
| 422 | `RIDE_NOT_ASSIGNABLE` | Ride is no longer `requested`/`searching`/`no_driver_found` (`current_status` says what it is) |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | `errors.ride`: `The passenger already has another active ride.` or a wallet hold error (`no_driver_found` rides) |
| 409 | `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` | The ride changed state while being assigned (e.g. a driver accepted it) — refresh and retry |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Unknown ride |
| 403 | — | Admin is not Operations / Super Admin |

query.description: Filter by ride status (e.g. matched, driver_en_route, driver_arrived, in_progress)
Contains match on trip reference, pickup/destination address, passenger, rider or driver name (max 100 chars)

request.description:
Rides in an active status with the driver's live position. Use it to fill the map on load.

Per ride:
- `driver_location` — `lat`, `lng`, `heading`, `speed`, `timestamp`, `updated_at` (ISO 8601); `null` if the driver app hasn't reported for 5 minutes.
- `driver_rating`.
- `eta` — `target` = `pickup` while `matched`/`driver_en_route` (minutes for the driver to reach the passenger), `destination` while `in_progress`; `null` otherwise. From the driver's last routed ETA, else a straight-line estimate.
- `stage_timestamps` — `requested_at`, `matched_at`, `driver_en_route_at` (driver set off), `driver_arrived_at`, `started_at`.
- `has_active_sos` and `sos` — `trigger_type` and `raised_by.role` are who raised it (`passenger` / `driver`); `raised_by` adds `user_id` and `name`.

Saves a ride (the one with an open SOS, if any) as `{{monitoring_ride_id}}` for **Get Ride Detail**.

request.description:
One ride for the ride details panel — same fields as a **List Active Rides** row, any status — plus:

- `driver_vehicle` — `make`, `model`, `colour`, `plate_number`, `vehicle_class`.
- `route` — planned pickup → destination route: `encoded_polyline` (Google encoded polyline, precision 5; decode with `google.maps.geometry.encoding.decodePath` or `@mapbox/polyline`), `distance_km`, `duration_minutes`. Cached per ride. `null` if the routing provider is down — fall back to a straight line.

Run **List Active Rides** first to set `{{monitoring_ride_id}}`.

item.description:
**Required Role(s):** Operations (Super Admin always has access)

Live map and ride board. Load with **List Active Rides** / **List Online Drivers**, then keep it live from the `admin.rides` WebSocket channel: `driver.location.updated` (positions, with `ride_id` and `eta` for drivers on a ride) and `ride.status.updated` (stage changes).

- **"Needs attention" badge:** `summary.awaiting_driver` from **Admin — Manual Assignment → List Pending Rides**.
- **Test data on staging:** `php artisan db:seed --class=MonitoringDemoSeeder` — active rides at every stage (`matched`, `driver_en_route`, `driver_arrived`, 2× `in_progress`), one with an open SOS raised by the passenger, drivers reporting their location every minute.

item.name: Admin — Scheduled Rides

request.description: Operations view: every booking still in `scheduled` status, soonest pickup first, with the passenger and `scheduled.reserved_driver`. Filters: `city_id`, `vehicle_class_id`, `from` / `to` (pickup time), `reserved` (true/false), `per_page` (1–100, default 25). Role: operations.

request.description:
Resolve or dismiss a case. Optional refund, **to the passenger's wallet by default** (`refund_method: wallet`; works for every payment method), or `card` (card payments only, always needs Finance approval). Card and wallet refunds share one refundable balance. `clawback_driver_earnings` (default true) recovers the driver's share of a wallet refund.

**Limits:** if this refund plus earlier refunds on the case is above the admin's limit (tier 1 ₦5,000, tier 2 and Safety ₦50,000, super admin none), or the method is `card`, the response is `202` and a refund request waits for a second admin; the case stays open.

**Errors:** `403` cannot work the case; `422` already closed, refund on dismissal, refund above what is refundable, a refund already waiting for approval.

**Late-cancellation fee disputes** (a cancelled scheduled booking, Phase 2 review): the refund goes to the **wallet only** (`card` → 422). The refundable amount is the fee collected minus earlier refunds, and the driver who received the fee pays it back (`clawback_driver_earnings`). A fee still owed as a balance due is **waived** instead, and only in full (another amount → 422).

request.description: Upholds a late-cancellation fee dispute. With the fee **charged**: ₦400 goes back to the passenger's wallet and ₦400 is taken back from the driver who received it (`driver_clawback_amount`). With the fee still **owed** (`balance_due`): send the whole fee as `refund_amount` and the balance due is waived. A waiver pays nothing back, so the case shows `waived_amount` (not `refund_amount` / `refund_method`). The clawback is skipped when `clawback_driver_earnings` is `false`. `refund_method: card`, more than the fee, or part of an owed fee → 422 on `refund_amount`. Tier refund limits apply as for any refund.

Closed without the item being returned → `unresolved`. `closure_reason`: `not_found`, `unclaimed`, `passenger_unreachable`, `driver_unreachable`, `other`.

Update all 5 tier configurations (names, thresholds, benefits). All 5 tiers must be provided with distinct tier_level values (1-5).

- `booking_fee_discount_pct`: percent off the **base fare**, 0–100 with up to 2 decimals; 0 means the tier has no discount. Show it as a number input, not an on/off switch.
- `exclusive_promotions_enabled`: whether the tier can use tier-only promos (promos with `min_tier_level` above 1). Optional: leave it out and the stored value is kept.

**Required Role:** Operations or Super Admin

request.description: The flag with evidence, driver (and city), passenger, ride, the driver's earlier flags in 30 days, `route_map` and `history`. `flag.allowed_actions` says which actions the admin can take now (uphold, overturn, escalate, de_escalate, confirm_deactivation, verify_cash_taking); `flag.driver_status` is the driver profile's status (use it, not `driver.is_active`, to show a deactivated driver). `flag.deactivation` (confirmed_at, confirmed_by, notes, reversed_at) and `flag.cash_taking` (verified_at, verified_by, notes) appear when they apply. `route_map`: pickup, destination, `route` (encoded polyline the driver was measured against, `source` planned_route or straight_line), `corridor_meters`, `cancelled_at`, `cancel_point`, and `driver_path` (one point every 30 s with `seconds_after_cancellation`, `on_route`, `distance_from_route_meters`). Flags before 2026-10-20 have no route, cancel point or path. Example: seeded driver Funke Ajayi, moved to Level 3 by verified cash-taking. Level 3 flags have `deactivation_response_due_at`: until then (unless the driver disputes) uphold and confirm_deactivation are not allowed.

request.description: Uphold or overturn a flag, disputed or not. `notes` (10–2000) is kept as `review_notes`. An upheld flag can be overturned later (appeal; history reads "Overturned on appeal"); an overturn is final. Overturning a flag whose deactivation was confirmed needs a super admin (OQ-14) and reactivates the driver. Overturning the driver's latest flag sets their status from the remaining flags. 422 `This flag has already been reviewed.` / `Only a super admin can overturn a flag whose deactivation was confirmed.` An undisputed Level 3 flag cannot be upheld until the driver's 48-hour response window (`deactivation_response_due_at`) ends; overturning is always allowed.

request.description: Record that an admin verified the driver took cash for the trip (e.g. the passenger confirmed paying). Moves the flag straight to Level 3 whatever the earlier flags, and suspends the driver pending review. The driver then has 48 hours (`deactivation_response_due_at`) to dispute before the flag can be upheld or the deactivation confirmed (Confirm Deactivation). `notes` (10–2000) required: how it was verified. Kept in `flag.cash_taking` (verified_at, verified_by, notes) and history ("Cash-taking verified from Level 1 to Level 3"). 422: overturned flag, already verified, deactivation confirmed.

response.name: 422 — Already Verified

request.description: Permanently deactivates the driver behind a Level 3 flag: status `deactivated`, forced offline, removed from the live driver index, push sent. `notes` (10–2000) is **required**: the reason, returned in `flag.deactivation.notes` and history. A flag nobody reviewed is upheld in the same step with the same reason (history: "Upheld and deactivation confirmed"). After it: `sanction_action` `deactivated`, `deactivation.confirmed_at/confirmed_by`, `driver_status` `deactivated`, `allowed_actions.confirm_deactivation` false. Undo only by a super admin overturning the flag. 422: not L3, dispute pending, overturned, already confirmed, driver already deactivated, notes missing. A driver whose flag reached Level 3 has 48 hours (`deactivation_response_due_at`) to dispute before it can be confirmed, unless they dispute sooner (then review the dispute first). A super admin can confirm before the deadline; history then reads "... before the driver's response deadline".

request.description:
Create a new EV charging station. Stalls are auto-generated based on `total_stalls`. Requires admin (operations) role. `status` is optional (`active`, `maintenance`, `inactive`).

`city_id` is optional: left out, it is worked out from `lat`/`lng` (422 on `city_id` if outside every active city). `connector_types`, `power_output_kw`, `pricing_per_kwh` and `operating_hours` are returned on the station. Returns the same station shape as every admin station endpoint: `availability.queue_length` and, on each stall, `current_driver` `{ id, name, phone, vehicle }` (null when no driver is charging).

exec: if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') { return; }

request.description:
Station with its stalls in number order, `station.availability` (with `queue_length`), and `queue`: drivers waiting in join order.

Each stall's `current_driver` and each queue entry's `driver` have the same shape: `{ id, name, phone, vehicle }`, with the plate on `vehicle` (`{ make, model, colour, plate_number }`). `current_driver` is null when no driver is charging. A queue entry also has `reservation_id`, `position`, `battery_level`, `joined_at`, `wait_seconds` and `estimated_available_at`.

The top-level `availability` is deprecated: it repeats `station.availability`.

The saved example is "Yaba EV Hub" from `php artisan db:seed --class=EvStationsDemoSeeder`: two drivers charging, one stall out of service, three drivers queued. Run **List All Stations** with `search=Yaba` to point `ev_station_id` at it; the saved response is from staging (2026-10-21); a re-run gives new ids and times.

request.description: All fields optional. `total_stalls` adds stalls at the end, or removes the highest-numbered ones if they are free (422 `Stall N is in use…` otherwise). Returns the same station shape as every admin station endpoint: `availability.queue_length` and, on each stall, `current_driver` `{ id, name, phone, vehicle }` (null when no driver is charging).

Change station operational status. Valid values: active, inactive, maintenance. Returns the same station shape as every admin station endpoint: `availability.queue_length` and, on each stall, `current_driver` `{ id, name, phone, vehicle }` (null when no driver is charging).

Add or update stalls for a station. Uses upsert by stall_number. Setting a stall to anything but `occupied` clears its `current_driver`, `occupied_since` and `estimated_departure_at`; marking a stall `occupied` by hand starts it afresh (`occupied_since` now, no driver). A stall with a driver's reservation on it (pending review, reserved or active) can't change status: 422 on `stalls` (`Stall N has a driver's reservation…`), and nothing in the request is saved. Returns the same station shape as every admin station endpoint: `availability.queue_length` and, on each stall, `current_driver` `{ id, name, phone, vehicle }` (null when no driver is charging).
Real-time utilisation summary across all active stations. Shows occupancy rates, available stalls, and estimated wait times.
Permanently deletes an EV charging station and all its stalls. Fails if the station has active reservations.

request.description:
Paginated payout requests. Filters: `status`, `search` (driver name/email), `from`/`to` (date range).

`needs_attention` is `true` when the transfer outcome has been unconfirmed for longer than usual: approved for over 10 minutes without being sent, or processing for over 30 minutes without Paystack's confirmation. Show a **Check status** button for those payouts that calls *Check Payout Status (Paystack)*.

`attention_reason` explains the flag: `awaiting_otp` (Paystack is holding the transfer for an OTP; turn off transfer OTP in the Paystack dashboard, then check status; flagged immediately), `not_sent` or `unconfirmed`. `provider_status` is Paystack's last reported status for the transfer. Each payout has `bank_account_block` (`null` or `code`, `message`, `payouts_held_until`): disable Approve/Retry when set.

response.name: 200 — Rejected
422 — Not Requested

request.description:
Finance retries a `failed` or `reversed` payout; in both cases the money is back in the driver's balance. The job first checks the previous transfer with Paystack: if it actually went through, the payout is marked paid instead of sending again. Otherwise the money is sent again under a new transfer reference (`PAYOUT-{id}-2`, `-3`, …), as Paystack advises after a definite failure. Any other status → 422.

For a payout stuck in `approved` or `processing`, use *Check Payout Status (Paystack)* instead. Refused with 409 while the payout's bank account is on hold, under review or rejected (`code`): resolve it under **Payout Accounts** first.

response.name: 200 — Retrying
422 — Not Failed or Reversed
409 — Bank Account Under Review

request.description:
Finance's **Check status** action for a payout whose transfer outcome is unknown — show it when the payout has `needs_attention: true` (approved for over 10 minutes without being sent, e.g. Paystack was unreachable for every attempt, or processing for over 30 minutes without Paystack's confirmation). It asks Paystack about the payout's transfer reference and settles the payout. The driver's money stays reserved until the outcome is known, and a transfer Paystack already has is never sent twice.

| `outcome` | Meaning | Payout afterwards |
|---|---|---|
| `paid` | Paystack completed the transfer | `paid` |
| `failed` | Paystack failed or reversed it; the money is back in the driver's balance | `reversed` — use *Retry Failed Payout* |
| `processing` | Paystack is still working on it | `processing` |
| `resent` | Paystack never received it; sent again under the same reference | `approved`, then `processing` |
| `unknown` | Processing, but Paystack has no transfer with this reference — contact Paystack support | unchanged |

`provider_status` is Paystack's own status (`success`, `failed`, `reversed`, `pending`, …). The scheduler runs the same check every 15 minutes, so most payouts settle without anyone pressing the button. Paystack unreachable → 502 (nothing changed; try again). Not `approved` or `processing` → 422 with `current_status`. Audited as `payout.verified`. Role: finance.

request.description:
**Single Paystack webhook URL.** No auth — verified by HMAC-SHA512 (`x-paystack-signature`) with `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY`.

- `charge.success` with a `TOPUP-` reference → wallet top-up (credited once).
- `charge.success` (other) → ride payment: re-verified with Paystack by reference, amount and currency checked, then captured and settled.
- `transfer.success` → payout paid; `transfer.failed` / `transfer.reversed` / `transfer.rejected` → payout failed and the money returned to the driver.

Events are stored per provider + event id + event type. A fully processed redelivery returns "Already processed."; an event whose processing failed part-way is processed again when Paystack retries — every handler is idempotent.

200 — Already Processed (duplicate)

request.description:
**Paystack's transfer Approval URL** (Settings → Preferences → Transfer Approval). Called by Paystack before every transfer, not by the apps. No auth: the endpoint changes nothing and approves only what is already in our database.

- `200` approves the transfer, `400` rejects it. No answer within a few seconds blocks it.
- Approved only if `reference` is a payout's `gateway_reference` (`PAYOUT-{id}`, `PAYOUT-{id}-2`, …), the payout is `approved` or `processing`, `amount` (kobo) equals the payout amount, `currency` (if sent) is `NGN`, and `recipient` is the recipient code saved on the payout before the transfer started.
- Anything else, such as a transfer started with a leaked secret key or made by hand in the dashboard, is rejected and logged as critical. The reason is logged, not returned.
- Paystack doesn't document the exact shape, so every object with a `reference` is treated as a transfer: at the top level, under `data`, or in a list (bulk), up to three levels deep. All of them must match. `recipient` may be an object carrying `recipient_code`.
- A rejection logs the request's shape (keys and types, no values) for diagnosis.

To try it locally, send a transfer whose reference, amount and recipient match an approved payout (200). Change any one of them to get 400.
